target_customer: Offices and event hosts ordering group catering for 10 to 1,000 people
problem: Ordering catering was slow and unreliable; MobyDish promised online ordering with its own drivers and setup.

founders.name: Bruno Didier
founders.background_notes: Solo founder; in the food industry since 2012 per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering and dispatch software; the hard part was operations with owned drivers.

defensibility.rationale: Catering marketplaces and owned logistics were easy to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced action by incumbents; ezCater was an established marketplace.

market_need_then: Corporate catering demand was large but no dated demand evidence was found.

identity.logo: Logo compared by a Product Hunt user to Docker's whale

brand_strength.rationale: Moby plus dish pun; only a Product Hunt comment about the logo found; no press.

outcome_analysis: MobyDish stayed small and solo founded, ran a catering service with its own delivery fleet, and was later sold on terms that are not public. A founder account says an expected $2.2M term sheet fell through in 2017 and angels gave about $250K, with a Series A closed in December 2019, but these are unverified here. The outcome cannot be explained further from public sources.
notes: Funding unverified: SeedTable lists a roughly $120K seed in 2015-03 (YC, Zeno Ventures), about $250K angels in 2017 and a Series A in 2019-12 with no amount; CB Insights lists $4.47M. All aggregator or founder account snippets, so no rounds recorded. One thin post claims sale to CookUnity; unconfirmed, acquirer left null. Company site returned 503. Competitor search returned only modern aggregator lists. Location conflict (Austin per YC, San Francisco per CB Insights). Trademark first use 2015-07.
